elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates..." — express defence duty running to Customer and its Affiliates (Affiliate is a defined term at 1.1).

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "...from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)..." in favour of Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "Vendor's breach of Applicable Law", using the defined term at 1.2.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (d): "Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct"; consistent with the Excluded Claims definition in 21.3.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "Customer shall give Vendor prompt written notice of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall control its defence and settlement" — control expressly allocated to Vendor.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: "Customer's indemnification obligations, if any, are limited to third-party claims arising out of Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law." No broader Customer indemnity exists elsewhere in the Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) of the inserted clause covers third-party IP infringement/misappropriation allegations regarding the Services or Deliverables.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: the inserted indemnity contains no such exclusion, which is more favourable to Customer; the condition permitting the carve-out simply is not exercised, so it is not a defect.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion was inserted, leaving the indemnity broader in Customer's favour.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specification exclusion inserted, so nothing narrows the indemnity against Customer.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy ladder appears in the inserted clause or elsewhere; Section 9.3's reference to "the remedies required by Section 20.5" remains unsupported.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual Fees super-cap is inserted; Section 21.3 leaves indemnification obligations as uncapped Excluded Claims.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the single inserted paragraph delivers all ten preferred elements — defence and indemnity for Customer and its Affiliates, all four covered limbs (IP infringement by Services/Deliverables, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorised access to Customer Data, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), the notice/control/cooperation mechanics, and an express limit on any Customer indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

Fallback is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund backstop, no 3x super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met; the drafter's decision not to import the 3x super-cap correctly avoids capping obligations that Section 21.3 currently leaves uncapped in Customer's favour.

Minimal: for a missing clause a concise insertion of wholly new words is permitted, and the text tracks the model language without extras — no survival tail, no at-own-expense wording, no added damages categories or procedural boilerplate beyond notice, control and cooperation, and no words deleted from Sections 9.3, 19.5, 21.3 or 30.5.

Preserves intent: the insertion uses existing defined terms (Affiliate 1.1, Applicable Law 1.2, Services 1.7, Customer Data/Deliverables as defined in Section 1), aligns with 19.5's preservation of indemnities, 21.3's Excluded Claims treatment of indemnification obligations, and 30.5's indemnified-party enforcement and vested indemnity rights; no retained sentence is contradicted.

Residual point (not a defect in the elements checked): Section 9.3's cross-reference to "the remedies required by Section 20.5" is a pre-existing dangling reference that the insertion does not create but also does not repair. If the numbering of the new clause is not 20.5, conform Section 9.3 (or add the procure/modify/replace ladder) at execution so the termination trigger in 9.3 remains operable.
